label: D-54f3a2

defects.summary: In S5.6.7, the 'refused' arm launches no shim, so the per-launch loop does not run, and nothing checks that the coai-vh\<8> folder it reserved (QuestionRowLaunch.cs:101) or the row's scratch is gone. That arm would still pass with Release() removed from finally, although the table's Then asks for this check 'after each ending' (the Vibe twin ARowRefusedAtItsCopy_GivesItsOneShotFolderBack does check it).

The skeleton's deviations stay in the plan but are false for the delivered code: 53 says MustCarryNoFlags is 'not wired into Build yet' (it is), and 56 says the tests are placeholders 'each region says so' (no regions remain). The status line also cites only deviations 58–63.

Deviation 63 says the classes use 'Scopes and StandIn as AKimiConsultationScenarioTests has them', but the change actually moves them into a new shared KimiStandIn.cs and rewrites E5.4's AKimiConsultationScenarioTests to use it. That refactor is not recorded as such.

TheVectorsCoverKimi is a new test that duplicates the existing every-pair test TheVectorsActuallyLoaded_AndCoverEveryPairOfTheTable, which the plan names as S5.6.2 and which already covers the kimi pairs.
The failing arm of S5.5.2 builds its own exit-70 session_lost ProcessResult instead of reusing the existing PlayedKimi.Lost helper.
When the flag is missing, ArgAfter does not fail: IndexOf returns -1 and it silently returns args[0].
S5.5.1 checks --cwd only by the substring own/tree, not that it is under the check's own scratch root.
Decision 2 says each row's note carries the version, but the kimi web row's note does not name 2.1.1 (the version is only in measuredWith.version).

summary: The data, the planner arm, the flag guard (Leading and Flags), the vectors and the generated table follow E5.5/E5.6, and all 12 scenarios exist and pass with no new failures; the shared KimiStandIn is good reuse. One arm of S5.6.7 checks nothing about the disposal, the plan keeps stale skeleton deviations that are no longer true, and there is a little redundancy in the tests.
